newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to rule soon on Norwegian salmon import duty.
newsitem.headline: EU to rule soon on Norwegian salmon import duty.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to decide in late April or early May whether to impose a duty on imports of farmed Atlantic salmon from Norway, a European Union source said on Thursday.

But he could not confirm a media report that EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan was expected to recommend a 13.7 percent duty on imports of Norwegian salmon after a European Commission report accused Norway of dumping.
The source said that an EU anti-dumping committee was not expected to deliver its advice on how the EU should act until April 7 or 9.
"On the basis of this advice the Commission makes its (decision)," the source said. The Commission has the power to impose provisional duties for six months.
In September, the Commission said it was looking into Scottish complaints that imports of salmon from Norway were being subsidised and dumped, hurting the EU industry.
The EU executive decided to open separate anti-dumping and anti-subsidy investigations concerning imports of farmed Atlantic salmon from Norway.
The Scottish Salmon Growers' Association Ltd and the Shetland Salmon Farmers' Association lodged the complaints.
A Norwegian EU source on Thursday rejected the dumping allegations, saying that Norwegian producers were just more efficient that those elsewhere.
If the Commission decided to slap an import duty on Norwegian salmon, this would amount to a protectionist measure, he added. "We are of the opinion that we are more efficient than the others."

However, the Financial Times newspaper reported on Wednesday that a confidential report by Commission experts says that Norwegian producers have been selling salmon in the EU at less than the cost of production.
The report also said that Norwegian producers had been paid unfair state subsidies, causing prices to fall and Scottish salmon growers to lose profits, the paper said.
